intro: Color Palette generates a list of random hex colors right in your browser. Set how many swatches you want and get that many random 6-digit hex codes (like #1a2b3c), one per line, ready to copy into your CSS, design mockups, or test fixtures. It's handy whenever you need quick, throwaway color values without opening a design tool.
useCases: Generate placeholder colors for UI mockups, wireframes, or component prototypes
Create random hex values to seed test fixtures or sample data
Get a starting set of swatches to riff on when picking a theme
Produce distinct colors for charts, tags, or category labels during development
Quickly grab a few random hex codes without launching a full design app

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The tool runs entirely in your browser and generates colors locally. Nothing is uploaded or sent anywhere.

faq.q: What format are the colors in?
faq.a: Each color is a 6-digit hex code prefixed with #, such as #0a1f9c. The output lists one hex code per line.

faq.q: How many colors can I generate at once?
faq.a: You can request between 1 and 50 colors. The count is clamped to that range, and invalid or empty input falls back to a default of 5.
Each hex value is picked using JavaScript's Math.random(), so colors are uniformly random across the full RGB range. They are not curated for harmony or contrast.

faq.q: Will I get the same palette twice?
faq.a: Generation is random and not seeded, so each run produces a fresh, independent set of colors. There is no way to reproduce a previous palette.
